name: API keys for your own API
needs: let customers call my API from their own code
how do I store API keys safely
a customer leaked their key and needs a new one
summary: Long random secrets your users create so their scripts can call your API without a password. You show the key once, store only a hash of it, and let users name, scope and revoke each one.
need_when: Customers or their tools need to call your API from servers, scripts or no-code tools.
skip_when: Only your own frontend calls the API. Use normal login sessions.
Third-party apps act on behalf of users. That calls for OAuth, not pasted keys.

ways.title: Hashed keys in your own table
ways.how: Generate 32 random bytes with a readable prefix like myapp_live_. Store a SHA-256 hash, the last 4 characters, scopes, created and last-used times.
ways.tradeoff: Simple and safe. You build the settings page, scopes and usage tracking.

ways.title: An API key service
ways.how: Unkey or Zuplo issue, verify and rate limit keys for you, with per-key analytics.
ways.tradeoff: Fast to ship. Every API call now depends on their verify step.

ways.title: Your auth provider's machine tokens
ways.how: Some auth providers (Clerk, WorkOS, Auth0) offer API keys or machine-to-machine tokens tied to your users or orgs.
ways.tradeoff: One less system. Features and limits vary a lot by plan.

prompt:
Add API keys so users can call my API from their own code.

Requirements:
- Settings page: create a key with a name and scopes ([read], [write]), list keys (name, prefix, last 4, scopes, created, last used) and revoke.
- Key format: a fixed prefix like [myapp_live_] plus at least 32 random bytes, base62 or base64url.
- Show the full key exactly once. Store only a SHA-256 hash and look keys up by that hash.
- Accept keys in the Authorization: Bearer header only, never in the URL.
- Check scopes on every endpoint. Revoked keys fail right away.
- Rate limit per key, and update last_used_at at most once a minute.
- Log key creation and revocation in the audit log.
- Never log full keys. Add the prefix pattern to secret scanning if the host supports it.

Acceptance checks (run each and show me the result):
1. The database has no column that holds a usable key.
2. A revoked key gets 401 on the next request.
3. A read-only key gets 403 on a write endpoint.
4. A key passed in the query string is refused.
5. Request logs show the key prefix, never the full key.
acceptance_checks: The database has no column that holds a usable key.
A revoked key gets 401 on the next request.
A read-only key gets 403 on a write endpoint.
A key passed in the query string is refused.
Request logs show the key prefix, never the full key.
if_you_skip_it: A database leak hands out working keys for every customer, or a leaked key can't be shut off without breaking everyone.
how_derek_runs_it: Custody Journal's mobile app tokens follow the same storage rule: the database keeps only a SHA-256 hash of each token, plus an expiry time.
